Let
\[
x=r u,\qquad r\ge 0,\quad u\in S^3.
\]
Since \(\Delta\) is homogeneous of degree \(6\) and \(dx=r^3\,dr\,d\sigma(u)\),
\[
I_n=\int_{S^3}|\Delta(u)|\int_0^\infty r^9
\exp\{-n(r^8P(u)^2+r^{10})\}\,dr\,d\sigma(u),
\]
where
\[
P(u)=u_1u_2u_3u_4.
\]
Put \(r=n^{-1/10}\rho\) and \(\lambda=n^{1/5}\). Then
\[
I_n=n^{-1}\int_0^\infty \rho^9 e^{-\rho^{10}}
B(\lambda\rho^8)\,d\rho,
\]
with
\[
B(t)=\int_{S^3}|\Delta(u)|e^{-tP(u)^2}\,d\sigma(u).
\]

The large-\(t\) behavior of \(B(t)\) is governed by the coordinate hypersurfaces \(u_i=0\). The leading term from one such hypersurface is
\[
\sqrt\pi\,t^{-1/2}\int_{S^2}|\Delta_3(v)|\,d\sigma(v),
\]
because \(P(u)\sim u_i\prod_{j\ne i}v_j\) and the factor \(\prod_{j\ne i}|v_j|\) cancels. Since
\[
\int_{S^2}|\Delta_3(v)|\,d\sigma(v)=\frac{3\pi}{2\sqrt2},
\]
the four hypersurfaces give
\[
B(t)=\frac{6\pi^{3/2}}{\sqrt2}\,t^{-1/2}+\cdots .
\]
Thus
\[
n^{-1}\cdot \frac{6\pi^{3/2}}{\sqrt2}\lambda^{-1/2}
\int_0^\infty \rho^5 e^{-\rho^{10}}\,d\rho
=
\frac{3\pi^{3/2}\Gamma(3/5)}{5\sqrt2}\,n^{-11/10},
\]
matching the subtracted term.

The next term comes from pairwise intersections \(u_i=u_j=0\). Near such an intersection, with the remaining two coordinates \((v,w)\in S^1\),
\[
|\Delta(u)|\sim |v-w|\,|vw|^2\,|a-b|,
\qquad
P(u)\sim abvw,
\]
where \(a,b\) are the two normal coordinates.

The universal two-normal correction is
\[
\int_{[-R,R]^2}|a-b|e^{-a^2b^2}\,da\,db-4\sqrt\pi R
\longrightarrow -4\Gamma(3/4).
\]
Therefore one pairwise intersection contributes
\[
-4\Gamma(3/4)\,t^{-3/4}
\int_{S^1}|vw|^{1/2}|v-w|\,d\sigma(v,w).
\]
There are \(\binom42=6\) pairwise intersections. Also
\[
\int_{S^1}|vw|^{1/2}|v-w|\,d\sigma
=
\frac{\pi}{\sqrt2}+2-\sqrt2\log(1+\sqrt2).
\]
Hence
\[
B(t)=\frac{6\pi^{3/2}}{\sqrt2}t^{-1/2}
-24\Gamma(3/4)
\left(\frac{\pi}{\sqrt2}+2-\sqrt2\log(1+\sqrt2)\right)t^{-3/4}
+o(t^{-3/4}).
\]

Using this in the radial integral,
\[
\int_0^\infty \rho^9(\rho^8)^{-3/4}e^{-\rho^{10}}\,d\rho
=
\int_0^\infty \rho^3e^{-\rho^{10}}\,d\rho
=
\frac1{10}\Gamma(2/5).
\]
Since \(\lambda^{-3/4}=n^{-3/20}\), the required limit is
\[
-\frac{24}{10}\Gamma(3/4)\Gamma(2/5)
\left(\frac{\pi}{\sqrt2}+2-\sqrt2\log(1+\sqrt2)\right).
\]

\[
\boxed{
-\frac{12}{5}\Gamma\!\left(\frac34\right)\Gamma\!\left(\frac25\right)
\left(\frac{\pi}{\sqrt2}+2-\sqrt2\log(1+\sqrt2)\right)
}
\]
